title: ~300 JNIM Fighters Encircle and Attack Diabou, Gourma Province, Burkina Faso — 2 Killed, Cattle Looted
detail: On May 14, 2026, approximately 300 JNIM militants attacked the vicinity of Diabou, a town in Burkina Faso's eastern Gourma Province. At least 2 civilians were killed and several others injured in the assault. Two farm plots were looted and destroyed, and dozens of cattle were seized — part of the economic warfare dimension of JNIM's multi-province offensive campaign. JNIM fighters have been encircling multiple villages in the Gourma area, forcing residents to flee their homes. The attack on Diabou follows the devastating JNIM operations at Djibo (May 11, Sahel Region, 100–200+ killed) and Diapaga (May 12–13, Est Region, 50+ killed), demonstrating the insurgency's continued high operational tempo across Burkina Faso's eastern and southeastern regions. Gourma Province shares a border with Niger and is a key corridor for JNIM's eastward and southward expansion, connecting to the tri-border Liptako-Gourma operational zone. The large force concentration (300 fighters) is consistent with JNIM's shift from smaller cell-based attacks to battalion-scale operations observed since early 2026. Burkinabè Armed Forces (FAB) have not issued a formal response statement as of May 15, 2026.

title: ISGS Ambush Kills ~26–28 in Niger's Tillabéri Region — Deadliest Single Strike in Recent Months
detail: Around May 14, 2026, Islamic State Sahel Province (ISSP/ISGS) fighters ambushed a security patrol in Niger's Tillabéri Region, reportedly killing approximately 26–28 fighters in what monitors described as the deadliest single ambush in the region in recent months. The attack occurred near the area around Tongo Tongo — the same region where a 2017 ISGS ambush killed 4 US Special Forces soldiers. Zagazola Makama, a regional conflict monitor, reported 26 militia killed in the ISGS attack. Niger's security environment in Tillabéri has deteriorated significantly since the July 2023 coup expelled French and US forces; IS-Sahel Province has since operated with reduced surveillance and aerial interdiction pressure. Tillabéri has seen over 1,200 conflict deaths in 2025 alone per ACLED. The ambush occurs in the same week as JNIM operations against Burkina Faso (Djibo, Diapaga, Diabou) and Mali's ongoing Bamako siege, demonstrating the coordinated operational pressure across all three AES member states simultaneously. Niger's AES/Unified Force recently claimed to have killed 150+ militants in Tillabéri on May 6, but ISGS has demonstrated the ability to absorb such losses and continue high-tempo operations in the region. Exact date and precise casualty figures are uncertain; the event is sourced from a single regional monitor (Tier 3).

title: FAMa, Africa Corps, and Dozo Militia Conduct Search Operation in Sikere, Ségou Region
detail: On May 14, 2026, Malian soldiers accompanied by Wagner Africa Corps fighters and Dozo traditional hunters' militia conducted a search and cordon operation in Sikere village in Mali's Ségou Region. The operation is consistent with FAMa's post-April 25 counter-insurgency strategy of deploying combined FAMa-Africa Corps-Dozo units to sweep villages in the Ségou corridor suspected of providing support or shelter to JNIM fighters. The Ségou Region has seen increasing JNIM (Katiba Macina) activity as JNIM uses the region as a transit and logistics zone between its Mopti heartland and southwestern Mali. No operational results (arrests, neutralizations) were publicly reported as of May 15, 2026. The use of Dozo militia alongside Africa Corps personnel reflects the AES junta's 'all available partners' approach to counter-insurgency — however, the same combination of FAMa/Dozo units has been documented in the Diafarabé civilian killings (May 12–15, 2026), raising accountability concerns about combined operations in the Ségou-Mopti corridor.
